source_text:
Ἐγὼ μὲν οὖν τὸ ἴδιον ἐποίουν ὡς ἄνθρωπος εἰς ἕνωσιν κατηρτισμένος. οὗ δὲ μερισμός ἐστιν καὶ ὀργή. θεὸς οὐ κατοικεῖ. πᾶσιν οὖν μετανοοῦσιν ἀφίει ὁ κύριος, ἐὰν μετανοήσωσιν εἰς ἑνότητα θεοῦ καὶ συνέδριον τοῦ ἐπισκόπου. πιστεύω τῇ χάριτι Ἰησοῦ Χριστοῦ, ὃς λύσει ἀφ̓ ὑμῶν πάντα δεσμόν.
παρακαλῶ δὲ ὑμᾶς μηδὲν κατ’ ἐριθείαν πράσσειν, ἀλλὰ κατὰ χριστομαθίαν. ἐπεὶ ἤκουσά τινων λεγόντων, ὅτι ἐὰν μὴ ἐν τοῖς ἀρχείοις εὕρω ἐν τῷ εὐαγγελίῳ οὐ πιστεύω: καὶ λέγοντός μου αὐτοῖς ὅτι γέγραπται, ἀπεκρίθησάν μοι ὅτι πρόκειται. ἐμοὶ δὲ ἀρχεῖά ἐστιν Ἰησοῦς Χριστός, τὰ ἄθικτα ἀρχεῖα ὁ σταυρὸς αὐτοῦ καὶ ὁ θάνατος καὶ ἡ ἀνάστασις αὐτοῦ καὶ ἡ πίστις ἡ δἰ αὐτοῦ, ἐν οἶς θέλω ἐν τῇ προσευχῇ ὑμῶν δικαιωθῆναι.
thought_title: The true archives are Christ's cross, death, and resurrection
orientation: Ignatius is writing to the Philadelphians, urging them to repent into unity with God and the bishop's council, and answering those who demand proof from the archives.
pass_a_gloss: I therefore [on the one hand] was doing [my] own [part] as a man [who has been] fitted together into unity. But where division is and anger, God does not dwell. To all therefore who repent the Lord forgives, if they repent into [the] unity of God and [the] council of the bishop. I trust [in] the grace of Jesus Christ, who will loose from you every bond. But I urge you to do nothing according to rivalry, but according to Christ-learning. Since I heard some saying, that 'If I do not find [it] in the archives, in the gospel I do not believe'; and [when] I said to them that 'It is written', they answered me that 'It lies before [us]'. But for me [the] archives are Jesus Christ, the inviolable archives [are] his cross and his death and his resurrection and the faith through him, in which [things] I wish by your prayer to be justified. [Note: 'passible' means 'capable of suffering'; 'passion' means 'suffering/death'.]

choices.why: The word means public records or documents; keeping 'archives' preserves the legal/scribal image Ignatius is answering
ἐριθεία denotes self-seeking factionalism; 'rivalry' captures the competitive spirit without modernizing to 'selfish ambition'
The coined compound χριστομαθία pairs with χριστιανισμός; a hyphenated rendering keeps the coinage visible and literal
ἄθικτος means untouched, not to be violated; 'inviolable' conveys the sacred untouchability of the cross, death, and resurrection
The passive infinitive of δικαιόω in a theological context carries the sense of being vindicated or declared righteous; 'justified' keeps the Pauline resonance

pass_b_english: For my part, I was doing what belonged to me as a person fitted for unity. But where there is division and anger, God does not dwell. The Lord forgives all who repent, if they repent into the unity of God and the council of elders under the bishop. I trust in the grace of Jesus Christ, who will release every bond from you.

I urge you to do nothing out of rivalry, but according to the teaching of Christ. For I heard some people saying, "Unless I find it in the ancient records, I do not believe it in the gospel." And when I said to them, "It is written," they answered me, "That is disputed." But for me, the ancient records are Jesus Christ; the inviolable ancient records are his cross and his death and his resurrection and the faith that is through him. In these I want to be justified through your prayer.

problems.ruling: Same error: ἀρχεῖα as 'archives' misleads; Ignatius contrasts written records with living authority of Christ.

problems.why: κατηρτισμένος means 'restored,' 'mended,' or 'prepared/established,' not 'fitted together' (which suggests physical assembly).

The English makes clear these are opponents' words, but 'some' hides that these are the false teachers/opponents Ignatius opposes. The brief marks sections 5.8 as 'Opponents' views paraphrased or quoted indirectly.' The English should signal these are opponents, not just 'some' people.

edits.new: For I heard some of them saying, "Unless I find it in the authorities, I do not believe it in the gospel." And when I said to them, "It is written," they answered me, "It is set forth."

fixed: The speaker attribution issue is already resolved: the English says 'For I heard some of them saying,' which identifies the opponents as the speakers.

The 'It is written' issue is not a mistranslation: the source has γέγραπται, which means 'It is written,' and the English correctly renders it. The note about opponents appealing to written documents is a commentary issue, not a translation error.
The 'passible' glossary issue is not present in the English text; it appears to be a note about a term not used in this passage.
